Claudia Conway's Parents, Kellyanne and George, Plan to Quit Their Jobs After She Tweeted About Emancipation
"I’m officially pushing for emancipation."
By
Jewel Wicker
August 24, 2020
Stefani Reynolds/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images
Kellyanne Conway,
senior counselor to President Donald Trump
, and her husband, George Conway, part of the Lincoln Project, have
both announced
plans to step away from their jobs after
Claudia Conway
,
their 15-year-old daughter
, tweeted that she planned to seek emancipation. The teenager
alleged
“years of childhood trauma and abuse,” citing it as the reason for her decision.
Neither of Claudia's parents have publicly commented on the allegations. Kellyanne currently serves as a counselor for Trump in the White House and previously served as his campaign manager. George is a conservative lawyer who cofounded the Lincoln Project, an
anti-Trump group
of Republicans who are
trying to motivate
more Republicans to elect Democratic presidential nominee Joe Biden.
“i’m officially pushing for emancipation,” Claudia wrote on Saturday. “buckle up because this is probably going to be public one way or another, unfortunately. welcome to my life.”

devastated
” by news that her mom would be speaking at the Republican National Convention this week.

On Sunday, George
tweeted
that he would be stepping away from his current work to focus on his family.
“So I’m withdrawing from @ProjectLincoln to devote more time to family matters. And I’ll be taking a Twitter hiatus,” he said. In a
statement
released Sunday night
, Kellyanne said she will transition from her role as senior counselor to the president at the end of the month. Referencing her husband’s announcement, she said, “We disagree about plenty but we are united on what matters most: the kids.”
X content
This content can also be viewed on the site it

from.
In recent months, Claudia Conway has publicly criticized the political views of both of her parents. She’s also been
outspoken
about social justice causes such as Black Lives Matter and the death of Breonna Taylor.
Claudia has also made supportive comments about her personal relationship with her parents, including in an interview with
Insider
, which the outlet says was approved and attended by George.
“They are the most generous, most well-educated people I have ever met,” Claudia said during the interview. “I look up to them and want nothing but success and good fortune for them. They are my parents and that trumps all — no pun intended.” In the same interview, Claudia accused her mother of trying to get her to delete her TikTok account. She said she “respectfully declined” to do so.
More recently, though, Claudia
has
accused
her parents of trying to silence her and delete her social media accounts. When George tweeted that he did not consent to journalists interviewing his children, all four of whom are minors, Claudia responded on the social media platform.
“You’re just mad that I’m finally getting my voice heard. Sorry your marriage failed,” she wrote in a since-deleted tweet,
according to a report from Complex before the tweet was deleted
.

Despite the news that her parents have resigned from their current positions, Claudia has stated that she plans to continue to push for emancipation. She captioned a TikTok video response to the recent news as “the power i hold - i— they think this is gonna stop me from getting emancipated? NANSHAJAB BYE”

Claudia has also been vocal in speaking out against people trying to turn her life into a political attack on her parents. On August 6,
she tweeted
, “TO ALL JOURNALISTS/REPORTERS/ANYONE IN THE MEDIA: DO NOT USE MY TRAUMA AS A MEANS FOR PUBLICITY OR PROFIT. IT’S SICKENING. I AM 15 YEARS OLD. EXPLOITING A MINOR PUBLICLY IS DISGUSTING.”
On Sunday, she posted that she would be taking a social media break,
writing
, “this is becoming way too much so i am taking a mental health break from social media. see y’all soon. thank you for the love and support. no hate to my parents please.”
